final_message:
I built `buildPickList` in `src/pickList.ts` test-first. All 34 tests in `bun test` pass and everything is committed, one commit per step.

**How I worked:** The test list sits at the top of `src/pickList.test.ts` and every item is now checked off. For each item I wrote one test, watched it fail, then made it pass. There were a few exceptions:
- **Two items in one step:** "no stock" and "partial stock" went in together, because the same change fixed both.
- **Tests that passed right away:** "blank lines and comments ignored", "stock used up by earlier orders", "same-bin picks keep their order", "stock not modified", "empty lots give no picks" and the spec example already passed when written. The code already handled them, so they guard against regressions rather than drive new code.

I added three items to the list along the way: aisles with stock but no picks don't count in the serpentine, a lot with quantity 0 gives no pick, and an end-to-end test using the example from the spec.

**Two judgement calls on the format errors:**
- **"First problem from the top":** an empty order is only noticed after the lines below it have been read, yet it can be the earliest problem. So the parser collects every problem and throws the one with the lowest line number. For example, in `ORDER 1001` / `OLIVE-500 x0`, the error points at the `ORDER` line, because a malformed line doesn't count as an item line.
- **Spacing:** `ORDER 1003!` (no space before `!`) and `ORDER 10 03` are errors. `ORDER  1001` with two spaces is also rejected, because the spec only shows one space after `ORDER`. Several spaces before `!` and between SKU and quantity are accepted, as specified.

Only the last commit has the `Co-Authored-By` line; the earlier step commits don't.
